title: A framework for analyzing global Caenorhabditis elegans neural activity
content: Neurons represent changes in external and internal environments by altering their activity patterns. While coherent brain-wide patterns of neural activity have been observed in neuronal populations, very little is known about their dimensionality, geometry, and how they are correlated with sensory inputs. Here, we recorded the activity of most head neurons in Caenorhabditis elegans experiencing changes in bacterial or control buffer stimuli around their nose. We first classified active neurons into six functional clusters: two sensory neuron clusters (ON and OFF responding to addition and removal of stimuli, respectively) and four motor/command neuron clusters (AVA, RME, SMDD, and SMDV). Next, we estimated stimulus selectivity for each cluster and found that while sensory neurons exhibit their maximal responses within 15 s, changes in bacterial stimuli drive maximal responses in command and motor neuron clusters after tens of seconds. Furthermore, we show that bacterial stimuli induce neural dynamics that are best described by a hyperbolic, not Euclidean, space indicating hierarchical organization in C. elegans neural population dynamics. This space was 8-dimensional, with dimensions that aligned in one sensory direction (ON and OFF neurons), two motor directions (forward-backward and dorsal-ventral), and the rest of dimensions corresponding with unclassified neurons. Collectively, we show that C. elegans neural activity can be effectively represented in low-dimensional hyperbolic space and describe how sensory information is processed by the neural network.

title: Endosome-associated Rab GTPases control distinct aspects of neural circuit assembly
content: Neural circuit assembly relies on the precise regulation of cell-surface receptors that mediate signaling and adhesion. Endocytosis controls receptor activity and availability by internalizing and routing proteins through early endosomes to one of two main pathways: recycling back to the cell-surface or delivery to lysosomes for degradation. Rab GTPases direct receptors into these distinct pathways, but their specific contributions to circuit formation remain opaque. Using clonal analyses with null alleles, we dissected the roles of Rab-mediated trafficking to early, late, and recycling endosomes across multiple stages of circuit assembly in vivo. Our approach revealed that Rab5 and Rab11 regulate extensive and largely distinct developmental events, highlighting the pivotal roles of early endosome sorting and recycling pathways in circuit assembly. As neurons mature, both the spatial distribution and abundance of specific endocytic compartments change to reflect evolving trafficking demands. Our findings underscore how distinct post-endocytic trafficking fates are necessary to build neural circuits.

title: Designing optimal perturbation inputs for system identification in neuroscience
content: Investigating the dynamics of neural networks, which are governed by connectivity between neurons, is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Because passive (spontaneous) activity provides only limited information for estimating connectivity, perturbation-based approaches are widely applied in neuroscience as they can evoke underlying hidden dynamics. However, the characteristics of such perturbations have typically been designed based on empirical or biological intuition. To enable more accurate estimation of connectivity, we propose a data-driven and theoretically grounded framework for optimally designing perturbation inputs, based on formulating the neural model as a control system. The core theoretical insight underlying our approach is that neural signals observed in the passive state lack sufficient latent information, which leads to failures in the system identification. Perturbations reveal these hidden dynamics and lead to improved estimation. Guided by these insights, we derive a theoretical basis for optimizing perturbation inputs that minimize estimation errors in neural system identification. Building upon this, we further explore the relationship of this theory with stimulation patterns commonly used in neuroscience, such as frequency, impulse, and step inputs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework for neuroscience through simulations grounded in experimental paradigms, such as neural state classification and optimal control of neural states. Our theoretical analysis, together with multiple simulations, consistently shows that perturbations designed according to our framework achieve substantially more accurate system identification compared to the conventional, intuition-based inputs. This study provides a theoretical foundation for designing perturbation inputs to achieve accurate estimation of neural dynamics. This, in turn, enables reliable discrimination of neural states such as levels of consciousness and pathological conditions, and facilitates precise control of their transitions toward recovery from abnormal states.

title: Reduced dorsal CA1 activity limits retention of the temporal component of declarative memory in the Cntnap2 knockout mouse model of autism
content: Growing evidence implicates the hippocampus in the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder, particularly in the domains of social interactions and cognition. Yet, the mechanisms driving the hippocampal-dependent cognitive atypicalities in autism remain poorly defined. Here, we characterized how dysfunction of the CA1 subfield of the dorsal hippocampus drives abnormalities in critical components of declarative memory. Using trace fear conditioning in the Cntnap2 knockout mouse model of autism, we found that capabilities to retain the association of temporally distant stimuli (i.e. temporal binding) were reduced relative to wildtype mice. Fiber photometry and optogenetic experiments demonstrated that reduced CA1 activity during temporal gaps underlies this impairment, linking CA1 dysfunction to a deficit in long-term memory retention in autism. Using a relational/declarative memory task, we also revealed a deficit in flexible spatial memory, and a preferential use of egocentric learning strategy. This inflexible learning strategy resulted from an imbalance between memory system activity, promoting frontostriatal-dependent procedural learning instead of dorsal CA1/hippocampus-dependent relational/declarative memory. Overall, this study establishes dorsal CA1 dysfunction as a circuit-level mechanism underlying cognitive inflexibility in autism, providing a neurobiological framework for hippocampal-dependent memory deficits in the condition.

title: A Predictable Component of the Internal Tide on a Narrow Continental Shelf
content:
Abstract
Coastal internal tides are considered unpredictable: harmonic fits to depth‐varying baroclinic velocity explain little variance. We show the depth‐averaged coastal internal tide is predictable from astronomical forcing. On the inner shelf, coastal trapped wave (CTW) modes are approximately depth‐uniform, so depth‐averaging recovers their coherent sum at the forcing frequency, while multimodal interference degrades coherence in depth‐varying velocity. SUNTANS simulations of M2 ${M}_{2}$‐forced CTWs in the Southern California Bight produce coherent phase propagation over several hundred km, sustained by distributed generation along the coast. Applying a harmonic skill score to seven‐year ADCP records at three inner‐shelf sites yields a 35 percentage point SS90 ${\mathrm{S}\mathrm{S}}_{90}$ gap between depth‐varying and depth‐averaged projections. Tidal‐band motions are ∼28% of alongshore variance, ∼73% of it depth‐averaged and dominated by the trapped wave, not surface tides. Predictability requires a slope supporting CTW generation at the relevant frequency and an analysis variable capturing the depth‐averaged response.

title: Contribution of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation to Global Mean Sea Level Trends: Revisited
content:
Abstract
Three decades of satellite altimeter observations reveal a continued rise in global mean sea level (GMSL), with the rate of rise reflecting the combined effects of decadal variability and long‐term warming. By decomposing 30‐year running trends of reconstructed sea level over 1950–2019, we quantify the contribution associated with the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) to the GMSL trend during the satellite altimetry era. Our results indicate that, over 1990–2019, the PDO‐associated contribution to the GMSL trend is 0.45 ± 0.07 mm/yr. This contribution is mediated through steric sea level changes (approximately 0.09 ± 0.03 mm/yr) and ocean mass changes related to land precipitation, evaporation, and runoff (approximately 0.34 ± 0.07 mm/yr). After removing the PDO‐associated influence, the acceleration in 30‐year GMSL trends decreases by about 70%. These findings underscore the importance of accounting for decadal sea level variability to detect the secular acceleration associated with anthropogenic warming.

title: Repeatable Velocity Fine Structure of Lightning K‐Leaders From a Single VHF Interferometer Made Three‐Dimensional
content:
Abstract
K‐processes re‐illuminate lightning channels at speeds of order 107 m s−1, but measuring their three‐dimensional (3‐D) propagation velocity has required multi‐station systems available at few sites. An error‐isomorphism range inversion upgrades a single very‐high‐frequency interferometer (INTF) into a 3‐D imager: Lightning Mapping Array (LMA) sources are back‐projected so that both data sets carry the same systematic bias, and Gaussian process regression extends the sparse LMA ranges to all INTF sources. Applied to three K‐leaders in a Florida cloud‐to‐ground flash, the method reconstructs the channel far more densely than the LMA and yields time‐resolved 3‐D velocities. The three leaders retrace one unbranched channel and reproduce the same velocity sequence, re‐intensifying after deep deceleration, their first maxima falling within 25 μs at 2.7–3.1 × 107 m s−1, indicating that branch junctions are not necessary for organized velocity variation.

title: Symbiont‐Mediated Molybdenum Cycling Shapes Coral Skeletal Mo Isotopes
content:
Abstract
Coral skeletal trace‐metal compositions are commonly assumed to derive from seawater, yet the extent to which biological processes contribute remains poorly constrained. Here we present the first paired Mo isotope measurements of coral tissue, symbiotic zooxanthellae, and skeleton. All three compartments are depleted in δ98Mo relative to seawater, with zooxanthellae significantly lighter than host tissue. A strong negative correlation between zooxanthellae and skeletal δ98Mo, together with a negative power‐law relationship between skeletal Mo concentration and δ98Mo across species and reef environments, indicates a symbiont‐mediated control on Mo partitioning. Fossil corals further show systematic variability in skeletal δ98Mo associated with climate variability over the past millennium, suggesting that environmental changes modulate symbiont‐driven biological processes recorded in coral skeletons. These observations suggest that biologically processed Mo contributes substantially to skeletal composition and that coral δ98Mo may serve as a novel proxy for symbiont metabolic activity and its response to environmental change.

title: Modulation of Slow Slip Event Characteristics Throughout the Costa Rica Subduction Zone Earthquake Cycle
content:
Abstract
Slow slip events (SSEs) represent an aseismic transient slip mode that repeats quasi‐periodically, near or partially overlapping with the megathrust earthquake zone. However, the process of stress interaction between SSEs and earthquake zones is not clearly understood. Here, we apply an earthquake and SSE sequence model to simulate the interseismic variability of SSE characteristics, and compare to observations pre‐ and post‐2012 Mw 7.6 Nicoya earthquake in the Costa Rica subduction zone, including six SSEs from 2003 to 2012 and four from 2014 to 2019. Our model reproduces the slip distribution of shallow and deep SSEs, and predicts higher peak velocity and larger cumulative slip of SSEs late in the earthquake cycle. This variability arises from the reciprocal stress transfer between SSEs and the earthquake zone. Our study suggests that systematically documented variations of SSE characteristics may reflect the long‐term unlocking process on megathrust faults where slow‐to‐fast slip modes coevolve.

title: Weak Positive Discharges Leading to Lightning Initiation
content:
Abstract
Lightning‐initiating events in the Earth's atmosphere originate within compact regions of space with dimensions on the order of hundreds of meters. In the strongest events the associated current pulses propagate from positive to negative thundercloud charge centers at speeds approaching one tenth of the speed of light, a process referred to as fast positive breakdown. Growing observational evidence indicates that these discharges can also develop with much lower current magnitudes and substantially slower propagation speeds. Here we present a quantitative analysis of weak photoelectric feedback discharges (Pasko et al., 2025, https://doi.org/10.1029/2025JD043897) that provides an accurate quantitative interpretation of the available observations in terms of current moments, pulse durations, and positive breakdown velocities. Similarly to volt‐ampere characteristics in conventional discharges the photoelectric feedback discharges exhibit a threshold type quadratic dependence on applied electric field explaining observed broad variability of parameters of these discharges.

title: Hydropeaking Catalyzes Redox Reactions in Impacted Aquifers: A First Field Evidence
content:
Abstract
Hydropeaking indicates the sudden and frequent fluctuation of river stage caused by the operation of hydropower plants. This river alteration affects numerous physical, chemical, biological, and ecohydrological processes in surface water bodies. The impact of hydropeaking on groundwater hydraulics has been investigated only recently through modeling and experimental studies at multiple spatial scales. This study presents new hydrological and geochemical surface water and groundwater data providing the first evidence of the impact of hydropeaking on groundwater hydrogeochemistry. To interpret these observations, we propose a conceptual model where the rapid vertical oscillation of the groundwater table acts as a pressure‐driven “geochemical pump” impacting redox conditions in the aquifer. This work has important implications for better understanding of groundwater biogeochemistry as well as for nutrient and carbon cycles.

title: Petagram‐Scale Dissolved Organic Carbon Stocks in Alaskan Permafrost Soils
content:
Abstract
The pan‐Arctic permafrost region hosts vast amounts of soil organic carbon, a pool increasingly susceptible to climate‐driven changes. Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is a key component of this carbon pool. However, its stocks and fluxes remain poorly understood due to limited measurements and challenges of tracking subsurface fluxes across landscapes. Through continuous leaching experiments on Alaskan soil samples, we established a statistical relationship between the percentage of leached soil carbon as DOC (DOC yield) and soil total organic carbon content (TOC) (y = 5.11×−0.43, R2 = 0.59). After validating this relationship against literature data, we applied it to estimate effective permafrost soil DOC stocks in Alaska, yielding 1.72 (1.01−2.66) Pg C for the 0–3 m depth interval and 0.53 (0.24−1.00) Pg C for the active layer. Our results highlight the importance of the permafrost soil DOC pool, and the robust quantification method offers insights for future pan‐Arctic DOC release assessments.

title: Structural Compactness of North Atlantic Tropical Cyclone Seeds in Historical and Projected Climates
content:
Abstract
We examine how the structural compactness of North Atlantic tropical cyclone (TC) seeds responds to warming in ERA5 reanalysis and CAM5 simulations. In ERA5, comparing 1985–1999 with 2000–2014, developing seeds in the later, warmer period become slightly more compact and exhibit stronger mid‐level ascent and low‐level convergence, whereas non‐developing seeds change much less. In the historical CAM5 experiment, by contrast, seed compactness and secondary circulation change little across the same two periods. Under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 forcing, CAM5 produces fewer developing seeds, more non‐developing seeds, and lower survival rates with stronger warming. However, developing seeds become less compact even as their secondary circulation strengthens, while non‐developing seeds show stronger secondary circulation but little compactness change. Compactness remains a useful discriminator of seed development, but its climate response differs substantially between ERA5 and CAM5.

title: Resolution Dependence of the Climate Feedback Parameter in Km‐Scale Climate Models
content:
Abstract
Global storm‐resolving models (GSRMs) provide new opportunities to investigate the climate response to warming with explicitly resolved deep convection. However, the limited number of existing studies has so far precluded the systematic assessment of similarities and differences across GSRMs. Here, we compare the Cess sensitivity (the climate sensitivity estimated from the response of atmospheric radiation budget to uniform surface warming) of the ICOsahedral Nonhydrostatic (ICON) model with three other GSRMs and CMIP5/6 models, using AMIP and aquaplanet model experiments under uniform warming (+4 K). We find that the Cess sensitivity across GSRMs at their finest horizontal resolution ranges from 2.2 to 3.3 K, comparable to that of CMIP6 models. In ICON, the negative net climate feedback parameter and its longwave component both decrease with finer resolution, while the positive shortwave component increases. The resolution dependence of the longwave and shortwave components originates primarily from the tropics and the Northern Hemisphere extratropics, respectively.

title: Boundary‐Aware Separation of Vortical and Wavy Motions in the Ocean
content:
Abstract
With the recent popularity of the tide‐resolving and submesoscale‐admitting numerical simulations, there is an increasing interest in separating vortical and wavy motions in the ocean. The recently‐proposed dynamics‐based decomposition exploits the relative magnitude of the relative vorticity and horizontal divergence in Fourier space and proves efficient. In this decomposition, physical variables over non‐water regions (e.g., coasts, islands, seamounts) are filled with zeros following standard practice. This zero‐filling would adversely affect the accuracy of vortical‐wavy separation, however. To mitigate this effect, this study adopts a streamline‐following perspective. With physical variables projected along the streamline and dynamics‐based decomposition adjusted accordingly, we get a boundary‐aware separation of vortical and wavy motions. The potential usefulness of this approach is demonstrated through its application to data from a high‐resolution numerical simulation.

title: Morphological Characteristics of Tropical Precipitation Features Producing Extreme Instantaneous Rain Rates in GPM and DYAMOND Global Storm Resolving Models
content:
Abstract
The influence of the spatial organization of tropical convection on the production of extreme instantaneous localized tropical rain rates remains poorly constrained, both in observations and in models. Using retrievals from the Ku‐band radar onboard the GPM satellite, we identify tropical precipitation features (PFs) and quantify their morphological characteristics. We find that PFs that produce extreme instantaneous rain rates are on average larger and have a higher convective area fraction than the average PF. Further, PFs whose convection is more spatially concentrated generate more intense maximum precipitation rates. We compare these observational results to the output of four DYAMOND models. We find that, while there is some model diversity in how sensitive maximum rain rate is to PF morphology, the models all capture the general relationship between PF morphology and extreme precipitation rates.

title: Melt Production and Volatile Release From Thermochemical Mantle Plumes
content:
Abstract
Mantle plumes are thought to generate Large Igneous Provinces (LIPs), the largest outpourings of lava in the geologic record, which are associated with long‐lasting climatic warming events and mass extinctions. However, the controls on mantle degassing by plumes remain poorly constrained. Here we use thermochemical plume models to compute the melt production and carbon release from compositionally heterogeneous plumes that sample peridotite and eclogite. We show that plume behavior is governed by the balance between thermal and compositional buoyancy. While excess temperature primarily controls melt production, carbon release is dominated by eclogite melting at depth and is maximized at intermediate eclogite fractions. Despite similar melt production, purely thermal plumes release about half as much CO2 ${\mathrm{C}\mathrm{O}}_{2}$ as eclogite‐bearing plumes. Our results highlight the significance of thermal and compositional buoyancy and the melting effects of eclogite in connecting thermochemical plumes to LIPs and their climate impacts.

title: Quantifying Deep Ocean Methane Along the Central Chilean Margin
content:
Abstract
Cold seeps are dynamic seafloor environments that provide conduits for methane (CH4) to be transferred from marine sediments to the global ocean and, in shallow settings, the atmosphere. These seeps are ubiquitous along continental margins yet their spatial extent and impact on the marine carbon cycle are poorly constrained. During a research expedition to the underexplored Chilean Margin, we utilized an ROV‐mounted in situ CH4 sensor and multibeam sonar to map seep fields. We confirmed seepage at depths between 100 and 2,750 m at El Quisco Seep Site, Concepción Methane Seep Area, and Mocha Island Seep Area. Combining ship‐based and ROV‐based acoustic gas flare detection with real‐time dissolved CH4 measurements three different manifestations of CH4 seepage were identified, which enabled estimations of both sediment‐seawater gaseous CH4 flux (69.2 ± 11.2 t/yr) and near‐seafloor dissolved CH4 storage (1.9 ± 1.3 t) along the central Chilean Margin.

title: Predominance of Externally Mixed Black Carbon Over the Tibetan Plateau During the Asian Summer Monsoon
content:
Abstract
The mixing state of black carbon (BC) strongly influences its lifetime and radiative forcing over the Tibetan Plateau (TP). Previous observations, mostly conducted during the non‐monsoon season, suggested that thickly coated BC dominates due to long‐range transport from South Asia. Here we report near‐surface BC mixing state measurements during the 2021–2023 summer monsoons at seven sites across the central–southern TP. We find that BC predominantly exists as bare/thinly‐coated state (externally mixed), with fractions of 73.2%–93.7%, much higher than earlier reports (20%–60%). This mainly arises from suppressed transport from South Asia during the monsoon season and intrinsically slow coating‐growth over the TP. The prevalence of externally mixed BC implies weaker absorption enhancement and CCN activity. These results underscore the need to represent seasonal variability of BC mixing state over the TP in climate models.

title: Future Northeastward Shift of Extratropical Transition of Tropical Cyclones Over the North Atlantic in Downscaling Projections
content:
Abstract
Tropical cyclones (TCs) often undergo extratropical transition (ET) at the midlatitudes, becoming post‐tropical cyclones (PTCs). We combine a logistic regression PTC identification model with synthetic TC tracks and intensities from the Columbia HAZard model (CHAZ) to project future ET completion over the North Atlantic (NA). Projections are based on downscaled outputs from 12 Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models under three shared socioeconomic pathways (SSPs): SSP2‐4.5, SSP3‐7.0, and SSP5‐8.5. Future changes in PTC numbers largely follow projected TC frequency, while the ET fraction remains nearly unchanged. Despite this stability, the preferred ET completion region shifts northeastward. This shift likely results from weaker vertical wind shear, larger potential intensity, slower overall translation speed at the midlatitudes, and more northward TC genesis. Although storms move more slowly overall, an enhanced eastward storm‐motion component favors the northeastward shift, whereas a weaker northward component partially offsets the displacement.

title: First Observation of Four‐Band Ion Cyclotron Whistlers
content:
Abstract
Ion cyclotron whistlers are frequently observed in low Earth orbit, typically formed when right‐hand polarized lightning whistlers undergo polarization reversal at crossover frequencies. In this study, we for the first time report a four‐band ion cyclotron whistler event detected by Van Allen Probe A. We analyze their fine structures and propagation characteristics, presenting the first observational evidence of ion cyclotron whistlers undergoing multiple ionospheric reflections. Using spectral features of electron whistlers and four‐band ion cyclotron whistlers, we infer the vertical extent of four ion species. The results suggest that they exist at sufficient densities from specific altitudes up to the satellite to resonate with and absorb ion cyclotron waves: H+ from 400 to 500 km, M/Q = 2 from ∼900 km, He+ from ∼700 km, and M/Q = 8 from ∼800 km, respectively. This multi‐band analysis of ion cyclotron whistlers provides a new perspective on using them as diagnostic tools for inferring ion presence.

title: Unexpected Inter‐Annual Variability in Methane Emissions From Western Siberia’s Oil and Gas Sector
content:
Abstract
Methane (CH4) emissions from the oil and gas (O&G) sector are a major source of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. Russia is a leading CH4 emitter, with the O&G sector accounting for approximately 80% of its total fossil fuel‐derived CH4 emissions. However, long‐term emission trends remain unclear due to significant discrepancies between bottom‐up inventories and atmospheric model estimates. We utilized atmospheric CH4 and carbon dioxide (CO2) measurements (2005–2021) from the JR‐STATION in Western Siberia, Russia's primary fossil fuel‐producing region, to clarify O&G‐derived CH4 emission variability. Our analysis reveals substantial fluctuations contradicting monotonic trends in national inventories. While national data sets suggest only gradual changes, our observations show a sharp increase exceeding 40% by 2009, followed by a decline through 2016 to levels 20% lower than in 2006. Despite rising O&G production, our findings do not support a continuous rise in CH4 emissions, highlighting the necessity of long‐term monitoring to verify national estimates.

title: Reassessing Methanesulfonic Acid as a Sea Ice Proxy: An Example From the Weddell Sea Sector
content:
Abstract
Antarctic sea ice has declined since 2015, but placing this trend in a longer‐term context remains challenging. Ice core methanesulfonic acid (MSA) offers a potential record of sea ice variability beyond the instrumental period, yet its applicability in sectors including the Weddell Sea remains unclear. We present an MSA record from the Gomez ice core on the southwest Antarctic Peninsula and combine air mass back‐trajectories and satellite observations to reassess the MSA‐sea ice relationship. Trajectory and spatial correlation analyses identify the central Weddell Sea as the dominant MSA source. We show that traditional correlations with northernmost sea ice extent are misleading in this region due to spatially complex seasonal ice dynamics; instead, the timing of autumn–winter ice advance and consolidation influences MSA formation during the following spring–summer. These findings highlight both the complexity of the MSA‐sea ice relationship and its potential for reconstructing seasonal sea ice variability.

title: Local Generation of Plasmaspheric Plume Hiss
content:
Abstract
The statistical analysis of hiss waves observed in the plasmaspheric plume (Wu et al., 2026, https://doi.org/10.1029/2026gl121667) is significant for identifying nonlinear wave growth processes in the equatorial region. Because nonlinear growth rates greatly exceed linear growth rates, they enable the local generation of new wave packets in the equatorial region. These nonlinear growth rates are governed by the background magnetic field gradient and the frequency sweep rates of the growing waves. The spatial extent of the nonlinear generation zone responsible for the local generation of hiss is derived theoretically under an assumption that the increasing gradient of the dipole magnetic field gives a limitation of nonlinear wave growth. The resulting theoretical predictions show reasonable agreement with the statistical distributions of hiss‐wave propagation directions observed in the plasmaspheric plume.

title: Millennial‐Scale Deoxygenation in the Southern California Oxygen Minimum Zone Over the Last Glacial Cycle
content:
Abstract
Past variability of oxygen minimum zones (OMZs) provides key insights into future ocean deoxygenation. However, California margin OMZ records remain temporally limited, restricting evaluation of mechanisms across full glacial–interglacial cycles. Here, we reconstruct high‐resolution bottom water oxygen (BWO) over the past ∼140,000 years using redox‐sensitive trace metals from ODP Site 1017E in the Southern California OMZ. BWO was lower during interglacial intervals (Last Interglacial and Holocene) than during glacial periods (Penultimate Glacial and Last Glacial Maximum). However, BWO exhibits previously unresolved millennial‐scale fluctuations during the glacial inception, including repeated deoxygenation events approaching interglacial conditions. This variability cannot be explained by local productivity or temperature‐driven oxygen solubility. Instead, it reflects changes in intermediate water ventilation, likely driven by shifting contributions of North Pacific and Equatorial Pacific intermediate waters. These results demonstrate that BWO in the Southern California is highly dynamic and may have been primarily controlled by ocean circulation.

title: Radio Sounding Determination of Two‐Dimensional Plasma Structure Velocity
content:
Abstract
The Mars spacecraft Tianwen‐1 transmitted radio signals to Earth for its orbit determination. The frequencies of the radio signals exhibited sharp variations when an ICME passed through the Mars‐Earth signal path on 18 June 2021. These sharp variations were observed at different ground stations at different times. This was most probably caused by increased plasma electron density in the ICME sheath crossing the signal paths of different ground stations successively. The time‐lag information of the frequency variations is used to infer the two‐dimensional sky‐plane velocity of the corresponding plasma structure in this study. The result is compared with the in situ observations from the nearest spacecraft, STEREO‐A, and shows good consistency. The validated radio sounding method for two‐dimensional velocities of plasma structures is beneficial for characterizing complex flow geometry and transverse dynamics, and can also contribute to better space weather forecasting in the future.

title: Coherent Turbulence Signatures Preceding Warm Rain Events From Collocated Cloud Radar and Wind Profiler Observations Across China
content:
Abstract
Warm rain is plagued by a longstanding droplet growth bottleneck, one that turbulence may alleviate by enhancing droplet coalescence in the late condensation phase. Nevertheless, empirical observational support from multiple sites remains scarce. Here, we combine collocated nationwide millimeter cloud radars, radar wind profilers, Himawari‐8/9 satellite cloud‐top temperature retrievals, and surface gauges to compile 819 warm rain events over China during the warm seasons of 2024–2025. During the 2 hr preceding rainfall, reflectivity and turbulent dissipation rate (ε) increase simultaneously within mid‐to‐low cloud layers. Cloud reflectivity is found to positively correlate with log10ε ${\log }_{10}\,\varepsilon $ throughout the pre‐rain period, with maximum spatial coherence and statistically significant correlation coefficients occurring 48–18 min before rainfall onset. This pre‐onset window provides multi‐site observational evidence for coordinated turbulence–reflectivity evolution, consistent with the conceptual framework that lower troposphere turbulence modulates warm rain microphysical processes and advances rainfall onset.

title: Seasonal Shifts in Nitrogen Isotope Fractionation Regimes in the Leighton Cycle
content:
Abstract
Nitrogen isotopes are used to trace nitrogen oxides (NOx = nitric oxide (NO) + nitrogen dioxide (NO2)) emissions and nitrate formation, but their interpretation depends on isotope redistribution during NO−NO2 cycling. A key uncertainty is whether this partitioning is controlled by equilibrium exchange or Leighton cycle. We simultaneously measured δ15N(NO2) and δ15N(NOx) in Taiyuan, China, during winter and summer 2024. The isotopic difference between NO2 and NOx reversed from (8.2 ± 6.5) ‰ in winter to (−6.1 ± 2.9) ‰ in summer. Winter data agree with theoretical equilibrium fractionation, and EIE‐corrected δ15N(NOx) matched direct measurements, providing field validation that ambient δ15N(NOx) can be reconstructed from δ15N(NO2) under EIE dominated regime. In summer, 15N‐depleted NO2 showed that Leighton cycle isotopic effect (LCIE) can dominate NO−NO2 partitioning even in polluted urban air. These results indicate that the magnitude and variability of LCIE require further constraints and validation for interpreting nitrogen isotopes in polluted atmospheres.

title: Interpreting Air Temperature Trends Across the Antarctic Peninsula Between 1979 and 2025
content:
Abstract
The near‐surface temperature of the Antarctic Peninsula is marked by strong spatio‐temporal variability. In situ observations are scarce and therefore have limited spatial coverage. Furthermore, ERA‐5 reanalysis does not have a sufficient spatial resolution to capture the steep topography and other climate gradients of the peninsula. Here, we evaluate and use the regional climate model RACMO2.4p1 to demonstrate that the average warming in the Antarctic Peninsula, as well as over all individual ice shelves, has been statistically insignificant between 1979 and 2025. We show that significant warming between 1979 and 2025 is restricted to northern coastal stations. Peninsula wide significant cooling between approximately 2000 and 2015 is strongest in the east. Peninsula wide significant warming after approximately 2015 is strongest in the northwest. We show that temperature trends strongly correlate with sea‐ice concentration, leading to larger trends in observations near the coast.

title: Constraining Fault Kinematics and India‐Tarim Convergence Partitioning in Southwestern Tibet With Geodetic Block Modeling
content:
Abstract
How the convergent strain between the India Plate and the Tarim basin is partitioned by active faults and off‐fault deformation in southwestern Tibet is poorly understood due to limited knowledge of strain localisation and fault kinematics. In this study, we derive high‐resolution velocity fields for the southwestern Tibetan Plateau using both GNSS and InSAR observations. Using these velocity fields, we apply an improved block model to estimate the kinematics of major active faults in the region. Our results suggest significant strain localization along the Altyn Tagh‐Ashikule‐Yulong Kashgar‐Gozha Co fault system and the Karakoram fault, which form the western boundaries of the eastward extrusion of Tibet. We also observe significant oblique thrusting along the Main Frontal Thrust, with convergence rates increasing from ∼16.6 mm/yr at 74°E to ∼25 mm/yr at 86°E. Based on our coupling distribution and slip rate deficit model, we reveal the seismic potential of the major faults.

title: Quantifying Nighttime Gravity Wave‐Driven Mesosphere‐Ionosphere Coupling Over CONUS Using NASA AWE Radiance and GNSS TEC Observations
content:
Abstract
We present the first coordinated study of nighttime mesosphere‐ionosphere coupling over the continental United States (CONUS) from January through November 2024 using NASA Atmospheric Waves Experiment (AWE) airglow measurements near 87 km and GNSS Total Electron Content observations near 300 km. Coherent wave structures observed at both altitudes and high spatial correlations between their variances are used to identify strongly coupled events. Among 273 AWE swaths, ∼65% exhibit strong coupling during quiet geomagnetic conditions, compared to ∼23% during active times. The occurrence of strong coupling is negatively correlated with Kp and AE and positively correlated with Dst, indicating systematic modulation by geomagnetic activity. For strongly coupled events, GNSS‐observed TIDs preferentially propagate northward, whereas only ∼14% exhibit the classic southwestward propagation associated with Perkins instability. This northward preference is consistent with nighttime thermospheric wind filtering that favors poleward‐propagating gravity waves. Our findings establish a quantitative baseline for nighttime mesosphere‐ionosphere coupling.

title: How Can the MJO's Planetary Scale Kelvin Wave and Synoptic Kelvin Waves Move at Different Phase Speeds in the Same Large‐Scale Environment?
content:
Abstract
Equatorially trapped Kelvin waves can occur through the depth of the troposphere and beyond. Previous works have demonstrated that these waves respond profoundly to the background flows through which they propagate, leading to variation in phase speed and dispersion characteristics. Vertical variation in the background flow might allow for the waves to move at different phase speeds through the same geographical regions. This work creates composites of zonal wind, geopotential height, and outgoing longwave radiation anomalies to diagnose differences in the upper and lower troposphere between planetary scale Kelvin waves associated with the Madden Julian Oscillation and fast synoptic scale Kelvin waves routinely seen propagating through the MJO convective envelope. Results suggest coherent Kelvin wave structure with the MJO only in the upper troposphere, where Doppler shifting by the background flow over the Indian Ocean slows them down. Results show that the lower tropospheric MJO signal is characterized by trough anomalies both east and west of the convection in a pattern that cannot sustain Kelvin wave propagation. Fast synoptic Kelvin waves, in contrast, show Kelvin‐like signatures over the Western Indian Ocean in both the upper and lower troposphere, but the upper tropospheric signals rapidly weaken, leaving only coherent Kelvin wave patterns in the lower troposphere, which maintain the rapid eastward phase speed under the weaker background wind speeds observed there.

title: A Unified Quadratic Scaling Relation Between Potency and Local Earthquake Magnitudes for −1.8 ≤ ML ≤ 7.5
content:
Abstract
Quantifying earthquake size across scales requires linking physical source parameters to empirical magnitude measures, especially for microearthquakes where attenuation, scattering, and instrumental limitations complicate source characterization. We combine regional results with near‐source observations from the Tony Creek dual Microseismic Experiment, dense nodal data from Ridgecrest, and regional broadband data from San Jacinto to extend potency–magnitude scaling to local‐magnitude ML≈−1.8 ${M}_{L}\approx -1.8$. Bayesian spectral inference yields robust potency estimates across seven potency magnitude MP ${M}_{P}$ units and nine ML ${M}_{L}$ units. The combined data sets follow a continuous quadratic relation MP=0.040ML2+0.556ML+1.133 ${M}_{P}=0.040{M}_{L}^{2}+0.556{M}_{L}+1.133$. Synthetic modeling shows that source scaling, attenuation, and the finite Wood–Anderson passband can produce similar nonlinearity, although rupture‐scaling differences may also contribute. Despite sensitivity to observational and regional factors, the independent data sets are broadly consistent with the established quadratic relation, supporting it as a general empirical scaling over the investigated size range.

title: Enhancing fairness in climate action through policy packages
content:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02751-5

Achieving climate neutrality requires policies perceived as fair, with equity both between and within income groups. Here researchers evaluate the equity implications of different European Union climate policy packages and show how a mixed policy design can balance trade-offs between two equity dimensions.

Asymmetric responses of phytoplankton size structure across the track of Typhoon Yagi and the underlying mechanisms
content:
Abstract
Typhoons disrupt upper‐ocean dynamics through wind‐driven mixing and upwelling, often producing cross‐track asymmetry in the Northern Hemisphere. However, how such asymmetric physical forcing reshapes phytoplankton size structure remains poorly understood. This study integrates multi‐sensor satellite observations with in situ size‐fractionated chlorophyll a (Chl a) and nutrient measurements to examine the impacts of Typhoon Yagi (2024) in the northwestern South China Sea. Post‐typhoon satellite observations showed cross‐track physical contrasts: the right‐of‐track side exhibited stronger surface cooling (~ 3–4°C). In situ sampling on September 10 revealed strong biogeochemical contrasts across the track. Mean surface NO3−$$ {\mathrm{NO}}_3^{-} $$ and SiO32−$$ {\mathrm{SiO}}_3^{2-} $$ concentrations were higher on the right side, with the most robust cross‐track contrast observed for SiO32−$$ {\mathrm{SiO}}_3^{2-} $$. Total surface Chl a was approximately 2.7‐fold higher on the right side when all three left‐side stations were included. At T6, elevated Chl a co‐occurred with an independently identified frontal and hydrographic anomaly. Size‐fractionated Chl a indicated that fractions > 2 μm dominated on the right side, whereas the 0.2–2 μm fraction contributed approximately 70% at left‐side Stas. T2 and T4. Notably, near‐bottom total Chl a on the left side peaked at T6, coincident with an intensified offshore sea surface temperature front. Satellite imagery on September 11–12 captured a delayed surface Chl a enhancement. These results are consistent with cross‐track differences in nutrient availability and upper‐ocean physical structure associated with asymmetric typhoon forcing, while lateral advection and frontal convergence may have further modulated the observed Chl a distribution. These findings provide new insight into post‐typhoon ecosystem restructuring.

title: Macrozooplankton community structure and trophic interactions differ across a sub‐Antarctic shelf break, independent of Antarctic krill
content:
Abstract
The South Georgia continental shelf break is a highly productive and biodiverse region of the Southern Ocean, with abundant macrozooplankton forming the foundation of off‐ and on‐shelf communities. Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba) are a major component of these communities and can dominate total biomass. In this study, we analyze a new 10‐year timeseries of spatially varied net samples from summer campaigns spanning the South Georgia shelf region to examine patterns of variability in macrozooplankton species abundance on‐ and off‐shelf in the austral summer. We found total net catch abundance was similar on‐ and off‐shelf, with particularly high abundances when Antarctic krill were present. Overall trends showed on‐shelf to be more variable in community composition, and more likely to contain high abundances of Antarctic krill. Community composition in the off‐shelf environment remained consistent between sites and with time and was more species rich than the on‐shelf community. Our analysis further revealed strong statistical associations in co‐occurrence between certain taxa, which sometimes varied between on‐shelf and off‐shelf communities. In a number of instances, these associations reflect either feeding guilds (taxa with similar prey preferences) or predator–prey co‐occurrence. Overall, although community composition differed between on‐shelf and off‐shelf environments, these compositions appeared to be relatively stable in space and time irrespective of the presence or absence of Antarctic krill. This finding, that the macrozooplankton communities appear relatively resilient to intra‐decadal environmental fluctuations in abundance, has particular importance when considering the impact of rapid regional climate change and potential longer‐term changes in the biomass of Antarctic krill on the wider South Georgia pelagic ecosystem.

title: Plankton nutritional quality outweighs isotopic trophic position in predicting food chain length across oceanic gradients
content:
Abstract
The Eastern Indian Ocean exhibits a gradient from eutrophic nearshore to oligotrophic offshore conditions. The trophic structure of the planktonic food web in this region was investigated in spring 2022 using stable isotopes (δ13C, δ15N), biomass, and piecewise structural equation models (PSEM). Regional comparisons based on grouped stations showed that the equatorial zone was highly oligotrophic with the shortest food‐chain length (FCL = 3.12), while the Bay of Bengal had the highest δ15N baseline and widest trophic range (0.10–4.0). The Sumatra upwelling and seamount area were nutrient‐rich, supporting high particulate organic matter (POM), phytoplankton biomass, and top predators with longer food chains (FCL = 4.26 and FCL = 4.73, respectively). Isotopic niches were broadest in nearshore and upwelling zones but most constrained in oligotrophic waters. Using station‐level data, the PSEM revealed that nitrite and chlorophyll a influenced isotopic patterns and FCL through POM carbon‐to‐nitrogen ratio (C : N), while plankton C : N played a significant role in extending the FCL. These findings emphasize how gradients shape food webs and the importance of upwelling and seamounts in supporting high‐trophic‐level species and carbon sequestration in the face of climate change.

title: Environmental filtering and spatial structuring differ among body‐size and reproductive‐mode groups of microcrustacean zooplankton in hardwater lakes
content:
Abstract
Local environmental factors are considered primary drivers of lake zooplankton community assembly, yet the roles of landscape factors and dispersal processes remain underexplored. We examined 78 hardwater lakes across the northern Great Plains (Canada) to evaluate how local (water chemistry, morphometric, and catchment characteristics), regional (climate and land use), and dispersal (spatial and lake isolation) factors explain microcrustacean zooplankton community composition. The region spans strong gradients in climate, water chemistry, and land use, making it well suited for disentangling multiscale influences. Taxa were grouped by body size and reproductive mode to evaluate trait‐related differences in community–environment relationships. Ordination, spatial modeling, variation partitioning, and hierarchical partitioning revealed that local physicochemical variables, especially conductivity‐related ions (sulfate and chloride), were the strongest predictors of community structure. Sulfate was most strongly associated with small‐bodied taxa, while chloride showed opposite effects. Primary productivity and lake metabolism played secondary roles. Regional land‐use and land‐cover factors, indicative of terrestrial–aquatic coupling, had relatively minor importance. Climate variables did not emerge as significant predictors of species composition. Spatial structure and lake isolation suggested a role for dispersal‐related processes in endorheic basins, with asexual species more strongly shaped by spatial factors than sexual ones. Compositional differences within body‐size and reproductive groups were also associated with local urban and agricultural land use. These results highlight the value of trait‐based groupings for interpreting ecological responses to environmental changes and emphasize the need to incorporate dispersal limitations into bioassessment and water management in lakes under increasing environmental pressures.

title: Thermogenic methane emissions from a glacier‐fed river on the Tibetan Plateau
content:
Abstract
Climate change is increasing glacial retreat and melt in many mountain catchments, impacting biogeochemical processes and carbon fluxes. However, the potential for changes in methane (CH4) emissions, sources and pathways in glacial‐fed streams remains poorly constrained, largely due to sparse field observations. Here, we present three consecutive years of full‐season field measurements of riverine CH4 flux and stable carbon isotopes in the glacier‐fed Lhasa River on the Tibetan Plateau. Our results reveal that riverine CH4 fluxes rise markedly with proximity to glacier termini during the melt season, indicating substantial CH4 emission potential in near‐glacier river reaches. Diffusive and ebullitive emissions averaged 67 ± 33 and 183 ± 15 μmol CH4 m−2 d−1, respectively, demonstrating that ebullition dominates CH4 release. High labile dissolved organic carbon and depleted δ13C‐CH4 indicate microbial dominance in the non‐melt season, whereas enriched δ13C‐CH4 with elevated CH4 saturations and spatial gradients indicate thermogenic sources during the melt season. Collectively, these lines of evidence illustrate that intensified glacier melt mobilizes CH4 stored within glacial catchments and facilitates its release into the riverine system. This finding improves our understanding of CH4 dynamics in glacier‐fed aquatic systems and underscores the indispensable role of thermogenic CH4 in constraining regional riverine CH4 emission budgets.

title: In situ degradation of kelp detritus: Implications for coastal carbon cycling
content:
Abstract
Marine macroalgae (i.e., seaweeds) are crucial components of coastal carbon cycles and may be important contributors to marine carbon sequestration. Understanding the fate of macroalgal‐derived carbon in marine systems requires an understanding of the degradation dynamics of macroalgae across environmental gradients. Therefore, we conducted an in situ kelp tissue degradation study in Tīkapa Moana/the Hauraki Gulf, Aotearoa New Zealand to assess the longevity of carbon contained within Ecklonia radiata kelp tissues. We utilized a set of six study sites which represent a natural gradient in turbidity to assess the influence of light availability on kelp decay dynamics, kelp tissue composition, and kelp surface/biofilm bacterial community. We found that half of kelp detritus disappeared within, on average, 58.37 ± 7.9 d. Light availability did not significantly influence kelp tissue longevity, although the shape of the kelp degradation curves differed across the light availability gradient. Kelp tissues maintained baseline concentrations of photosynthetic pigments throughout decomposition, while C : N (carbon : nitrogen) ratio decreased through degradation time at all sites. Degradation was associated with increased alpha diversity of kelp epiphytic bacterial communities and significant changes in kelp epiphytic bacterial community structure. This research shows that kelp tissues persist on subtidal rocky reefs in Tīkapa Moana/the Hauraki Gulf for no longer than 4 months, and that kelp degradation involves complex biogeochemical transformations that are not captured by biomass loss alone. These findings have critical implications for assessing the carbon sequestration potential of kelp forests in Aotearoa New Zealand and beyond.

title: Topographic control of tides in the Ross Sea: eddy-like structures, bottom-trapped waves, and energetics
content:
Topographic control of tides in the Ross Sea: eddy-like structures, bottom-trapped waves, and energetics
Yue Xia, Hengling Leng, Zhaomin Wang, Craig Stevens, Chengyan Liu, Liangjun Yan, Xianxian Han, and Dake Chen
Ocean Sci., 22, 3145–3164, https://doi.org/10.5194/os-22-3145-2026, 2026
Around Antarctica, tides strongly influence ice shelves through both dynamic and thermodynamic processes, and also help form dense bottom water that drives global ocean circulation. Using a regional model of the Ross Sea, we identified three eddy-like structures along the slope that control local water and heat transport, which potentially contributes to ice shelf melting.

title: Systemic control and inter-organ communication of ovarian aging
content: Whether ovarian aging is intrinsic and unidirectional or dynamically regulated by systemic context remains an open question for fertility and women's healthspan. To address it, we developed a mouse ovarian transcriptomic aging clock (OvaAge) and applied it, together with published transcriptomic, epigenetic and pathway-resolved DNA methylation (PathAge) clocks, multi-omic analyses and reproductive outcomes, to new reciprocal heterochronic ovary transplantation and parabiosis experiments. Ovarian molecular age shifted in both directions: aged ovaries became younger in young hosts and young ovaries became older in aged hosts, and in each case the shift was partial across transcriptomic, epigenetic and pathway-resolved measures. Ovaries from 13-month-old C57BL/6J donors supported full-term pregnancies and live births at 17-18 months of age when transplanted into young hosts, but not when transplanted into old hosts, and young ovaries supported live births in 17-18-month-old recipients. Donor ovary age altered the transcriptomic age of the uterus in both directions, while young ovaries also lowered the transcriptomic age of aged liver and brain, identifying the ovary as an active node within an inter-organ aging network. Across unilateral and bilateral transplantation and parabiosis, an older environment increased inflammatory gene expression in the ovary, whereas a younger environment reduced it and increased mitochondrial and biosynthetic programs. Integration of methylation, expression and cell-type markers linked these changes to declining oocyte-associated programs and an expanding stromal compartment enriched for multinucleated giant cells (MNGCs). MNGC-rich regions formed a reversibly remodeled, focally aged niche with distinct spatial metabolic features, and a related macrophage expression signature was detected in human ovaries. Together, these findings identify ovarian aging as a modular, bidirectionally plastic process that is regulated by the systemic environment and point to tractable intervention points.

title: Linking H3K36me3 to transcriptional dynamics
content: Genes are transcribed in bursts as they fluctuate between on and off states, in a process modulated by histone modifications. The mammalian histone methyltransferase SETD2 is solely responsible for depositing H3K36 trimethylation, which recruits histone deacetylases and regulates histone occupancy. Nucleosomes are known to act as a barrier to transcription elongation and have been observed to impact elongation rate. H3K36me3 has been associated with long pausing sites in gene bodies and is implicated in reducing speed of successive RNA polymerase II. However, the role of SETD2 and H3K36me3 in transcriptional dynamics are unknown. Here we show upon SETD2 knockout and H3K36me3 depletion in murine C2C12 myoblast cells that overall gene expression is reduced and splicing fidelity affected, as 5' mutually exclusive exons are favoured over 3' ones. Furthermore, transcriptional burst size is reduced, while bursting frequency increased. A simple mathematical model suggests that the observed changes in transcriptional dynamics can be explained by less stringently controlled polymerase pausing in the gene bodies of H3K36me3 depleted cells.

title: A mathematical model of tumor growth driven by oxygen lactate exosome feedback
content: Solid tumors develop within a heterogeneous microenvironment shaped by coupled biochemical and metabolic processes. As a tumor grows, oxygen gradients develop from the periphery towards the core, giving rise to hypoxic regions. Hypoxia induces a metabolic shift from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis, leading to elevated lactate production. Experimental studies further indicate that increased lactate levels enhance the secretion of tumor-derived exosomes carrying proteins, mRNA, and lipids, which in turn promote tumor cell proliferation. Together, these interactions form a feedback loop linking oxygen availability, lactate accumulation, and exosome-mediated signaling. Despite growing experimental evidence for each component, the impact of this coupled oxygen lactate exosome axis on tumor growth dynamics has not yet been systematically explored from a mathematical perspective. It remains unclear how the oxygen lactate exosome axis affects tumor growth - impact of nonlocal effects. In this paper, we develop a mechanistic mathematical model to investigate how this feedback mechanisms affects tumor growth. We first consider an in vitro setting oxygen levels are spatially homogeneous and vary periodically in time between normoxic and hypoxic states, capturing key features of cyclic hypoxia observed in vivo. Numerical simulations reveal that exosome mediated feedback has a pronounced effect on tumor volume under chronic hypoxia. In addition, we observe that the tumor volume decreases as the period of cyclic hypoxia increases. We then extend the model to an in vivo framework by incorporating oxygen diffusion and consumption, allowing spatial heterogeneity to emerge. Simulations reveal that tumor cells in normoxic regions benefit indirectly from enhanced exosome secretion driven by lactate produced in hypoxic regions. Overall, the results show how spatially mediated metabolic signaling can amplify tumor growth and aggressiveness, and illustrate how mathematical modeling can increase understanding of non local feedback mechanisms within the tumor microenvironment.

title: Common cis-eQTLs do not explain chromosome 21 expression deviations from the ploidy expectation in Down syndrome
content: Down syndrome (DS) results from trisomy 21 (T21), the triplication of human chromosome 21 (HSA21). On average, genes on HSA21 are overexpressed at the expected 1.5-fold increase. A small subset of HSA21 genes is expressed closer to euploid levels. Could local genetic regulatory variation explain deviations from the expected dosage? Using the largest DS-specific transcriptomic dataset to date from the Human Trisome Project (HTP) and GTEx expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), we tested whether local genetic regulatory variation contributes to gene-specific buffering or amplification of HSA21 dosage effects in DS. We compared the bulk RNA-seq profiles of protein-coding genes, lncRNAs, and pseudogenes from whole-blood samples of 274 participants with T21 and 80 euploid (D21) participants. We filtered out genes with low read counts or high genomic repeat content and applied ploidy correction to the differential expression analysis. We found 13 genes that differed significantly from the expected fold change. We cross-referenced GTEx whole-blood eQTLs (cis window 1 {+/-} Mb) with the 13 deviating genes. A common cis-eQTL was detected for 8 of the 10 testable genes. However, 59 of 99 HSA21 genes that had the expected fold change had significant cis-eQTLs. Additionally, T21 participants carry the eQTL alleles at similar frequencies to GTEx donors. Therefore, cis-eQTLs explain differences between people with T21, not the difference between T21 and D21. Overall, common cis-regulatory variation acts on HSA21 genes in T21 as it does in euploid blood, but it does not explain which genes deviate from the ploidy expectation.

title: An epigenetic palimpsest: the King penguin's blood methylome reveals conserved hematopoietic ageing
content: Age-associated DNA methylation is conserved across vertebrates, but whether epigenetic ageing reflects cellular ageing programmes or age-dependent shifts in cell composition remains unresolved. Here, using 126 whole-blood methylomes from known-age King penguins (Aptenodytes patagonicus), we exploit a vertebrate system in which nucleated erythrocytes dominate peripheral blood, minimizing the influence of leukocyte heterogeneity. We identify a core set of 409 ageing-associated genes showing lifelong, clock-like methylation change. These genes are strongly enriched for regulators of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) function and niche communication. Integration of methylome, transcriptome and chromatin-accessibility data reveals that many of the strongest ageing signals derive from genes inactive in mature erythrocytes, consistent with the persistence of epigenetic states from ancestral hematopoietic progenitors. A comparison with methylation profiles from 1,501 humans identified a conserved cross-species subset of ageing genes, and a human epigenetic age model constructed solely from orthologues of penguin ageing genes predicts chronological age with high accuracy while remaining largely insensitive to blood cell composition. We propose that blood epigenetic ageing signatures contain a long-lived cellular memory of stem-cell ageing, that may represent an evolutionarily ancient layer of the vertebrate ageing process.

title: When can site-specific glycoform compositions resolve biosynthetic rates?
content: Mass spectrometry measures site-specific glycoform compositions, but when these measurements can resolve upstream biosynthetic rates remains unclear. We assess whether small changes in effective rates, each representing the processing capacity of a group of biosynthetic reactions, can be distinguished near specified baseline rates with secretion held fixed. Because proportions sum to one, m jointly normalised glycoform classes provide at most m-1 independent quantities. Distinguishing changes in k rates therefore requires at least k+1 classes, although this count alone does not ensure identifiability. In a canonical N-glycan network with eight rates, exhaustive evaluation of nine-class panels identified panels that could locally distinguish all eight rates. Among these panels, class choice changed the allowable measurement error by approximately 18-fold for the same target uncertainty in inferred rates. A separate simulation within the fixed network showed that estimating rate-change combinations with weaker composition responses reduced bias but amplified measurement noise. We applied the framework to plasma data from 40 controls and 70 patients across 14 inherited glycosylation-disorder groups. A prespecified composition score for the expected pathway disturbance ranked among the top two in 13 of 14 groups. Network responses linked observed composition shifts to biosynthetic reaction classes. Expanding site models from five to eight reaction classes improved control-composition fit but reduced the number of sites at which all modelled rates were locally distinguishable and increased noise sensitivity. Rate inference thus requires sufficient panel size, separable rate responses, adequate measurement precision and a model that fits the composition. These requirements guide measurement design and help determine whether compositions support pathway-level interpretation or individual-rate inference.

title: A tissue time machine to forward-predict single-timepoint data applied to tuberculosis granulomas
content: Recent advances have improved understanding of infection; however many detailed datasets are based on single timepoints post-infection and cannot generate longitudinal insights needed to predict infection outcomes. For example, pulmonary infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) initiates a complex system of immune and bacterial interactions that leads to granuloma formation, yet single snapshots in time need elaboration long-term. We develop a new approach, the tissue time machine, applied to predict outcomes of non-human primate granulomas from initiation to endpoint using single timepoint tissue datasets including high-dimensional spatial features. This involves identifying granuloma digital partners, simulations most closely resembling real granulomas from a virtual library of over 50,000. By analyzing digital partners, we predict infection outcomes of 22/28 granulomas, and that Mtb-specific, IFN-{gamma}-producing T cell recruitment rates influence uncertainty for the 6/28. This method is applicable to any system that allows for mechanistic predictions over time using heterogeneous, incomplete, and high-dimensional datasets.

title: Engineered regulatory states resolve context-dependent genetics in macular degeneration
content: The effects of many genes and disease-associated variants remain hidden in standard cellular models, limiting functional interpretation. Here we engineer regulatory states via CRISPR activation of transcription factors (TFs) in human RPE-1 cells, a model for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Multiome Perturb-seq profiling of single-TF perturbations identified regulators that selectively opened chromatin at AMD GWAS variants inaccessible in resting RPE-1. Priming of partner motifs in chromatin made accessible by single-TF perturbations predicted TF pairs generating emergent transcriptional states in combinatorial Perturb-seq, providing a design principle for selecting informative interactions. Distinct TF pairs also showed variable convergence between polygenic AMD signals and Mendelian retinal disease genes, supporting an omnigenic model shaped by regulatory states. Finally, Mosaic, a chromatin-informed model of TF interaction phenotypes, nominated out-of-sample regulators, including a higher-order combination with experimentally validated emergent effects on AMD-associated programs. Engineered regulatory states thus bring hidden disease biology within experimental reach.

title: Excessive sample reagent incubation time increases the risk of false rifampin resistance results in Xpert(R) MTB/RIF Ultra tests performed on paucibacillary Mycobacterium tuberculosis sputum.
content: A high rate of false rifampicin resistance (RIF-R) was recently reported in paucibacillary sputum samples tested with the Xpert(R) MTB/RIF Ultra (Ultra) assay. However, 96% of the studied facilities started the test 8 - 12 hours after addition of sample reagent (SR), exceeding the manufacturers recommended limit of 4 hours. Assessed whether excessive long SR incubation could lead to similar false RIF-R results in paucibacillary samples in a reference laboratory setting. We evaluated the performance of the Ultra assay following incubation of TB-negative sputum spiked with 300 CFU/mL and 100,000 CFU/mL levels of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) H37Rv in SR for different durations (15 min to 24hrs.) at different temperatures (-20 to 370C) to determine the effect on RIF result calls. No false RIF-R results were observed in these samples with 105 CFU/mL Mtb at any of the conditions tested, even when they deviated largely from recommended limits. Similarly, freezing the 300 CFU/mL SR treated samples at minus 200C for 18 h also prevented the development of false RIF-R results. However, sputum spiked with 300 CFU/ml Mtb, produced false RIF-R calls at longer incubation times and higher incubation temperatures than are recommended by the manufacturer. Approximately half of the results displayed melt patterns consistent with hetero-resistance, indicating SR-induced mutagenesis in a wild-type background. This study demonstrates that extended off-label SR incubation of paucibacillary specimens beyond the recommended 4-hour limit can generate false RIF-R results. Freezing paucibacillary specimens in SR may mitigate this risk although it is not yet an approved procedure.

title: Disruption of cAMP Signalling and RNA Regulation Confers Cefiderocol Resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii
content: Cefiderocol is a siderophore-conjugated cephalosporin used to treat severe multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections. Its recent prioritisation for US national preparedness underscores its clinical importance, yet resistance can emerge despite apparent in vitro susceptibility. Here, we identify two regulatory routes to cefiderocol resistance in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB): mutation of the cAMP-producing adenylate cyclase CavA and truncation of the glycine-rich RNA-binding domain of the post-transcriptional regulator Hfq. These variants occurred in contemporary clinical isolates, conferred resistance in a murine CRAB lung-infection model and imposed minimal fitness costs. In Escherichia coli, deletion of the CavA orthologue cyaA increased competitive fitness during sub-inhibitory cefiderocol exposure. Hfq-CLASH and integrated omics revealed Hfq-dependent regulation of Fur-associated iron homeostasis in A. baumannii. Under iron limitation, truncated-Hfq induced a defence-primed state that attenuated siderophore uptake and reduced cefiderocol activity. These findings identify bacterial regulatory state and iron availability as determinants of cefiderocol susceptibility, with implications for resistance surveillance and susceptibility testing.

title: Anti-trypanosomal activity and target validation of the M17 leucyl-aminopeptidase inhibitor DDD00057570 in Trypanosoma cruzi
content: Background: Chagas disease, caused by the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, affects six to seven million people, and its treatment still relies on two drugs introduced more than fifty years ago, both of limited efficacy and poorly tolerated. The major acidic M17 leucyl-aminopeptidase of T. cruzi is expressed in all developmental stages of the parasite and has been proposed as a drug target, but it has not been pharmacologically validated. Methodology/Principal Findings: We assessed DDD00057570, a compound originally identified as an inhibitor of the orthologue enzyme of Leishmania major, against the recombinant T. cruzi enzyme and against the parasite. The compound inhibited the recombinant enzyme with an IC50 of 2.7 {+/-} 0.9 {micro}M and reduced the proliferation of insect-stage epimastigotes, with a half-maximal effective concentration of 3.7 {+/-} 1.1 {micro}M. Parasites engineered to overexpress the enzyme were twice as resistant to the compound as wild-type parasites, indicating that the enzyme is a primary target in the living parasite. Treatment increased the proportion of epimastigotes with fragmented DNA. In infected mammalian cells, the compound reduced the release of trypomastigotes, the stage responsible for dissemination in the mammalian host, with a half-maximal effective concentration of 1.3 {+/-} 0.6 {micro}M, while its half-maximal cytotoxic concentration on CHO-K1 mammalian host cells was 41.5 {+/-} 3.9 {micro}M, resulting in a selectivity index of approximately 32. Conclusions/Significance: These results validate the major M17 leucyl-aminopeptidase as a drug target in T. cruzi through target overexpression, and identify DDD00057570 as a selective lead structure warranting mechanistic, pharmacokinetic and in vivo studies toward a new treatment for Chagas disease.

title: Reversible fixation of microbial cells for targeted genomics
content: Phylogeny- or activity-based fluorescent labelling of microorganisms coupled with fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) is a powerful approach to rapidly isolate cells of interest from complex communities for targeted genomics. However, the method has not been widely adopted because standard paraformaldehyde or ethanol fixation procedures hamper nucleic acid recovery and/or long-term sample storage. Here, we present dithiobis(succinimidyl propionate) (DSP) as a reversible fixative for microbial cells that enables fluorescence imaging and DNA extraction and amplification for sequencing. DSP fixation is compatible with widely used fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) approaches and bioorthogonal non-canonical amino acid tagging, and can be applied to diverse sample types, where it consistently performed as well as paraformaldehyde. Furthermore, high-quality genomes were obtained from individual and multiple bacterial cells selectively extracted from complex samples using FISH-FACS. Thus, DSP is a dual-use fixative for microbiome imaging and sequencing, improving targeted microbial genomics.

title: Viral dispersal drives changes in population composition
content: In an acute viral infection, a small seeding population expands rapidly over several orders of magnitude, then declines. This vast population growth is accompanied by spatial expansion as infection spreads to new anatomical sites within the host. Evolutionary theory predicts that spatially expanding populations experience more extreme stochastic losses of genetic diversity than spatially unstructured populations. To test this prediction in the context of viral dynamics, we evaluated the impact of spatial expansion on viral population genetic structure and assessed how modulators of viral dispersal affected this structure. To this end, we developed a means of implementing the spatial expansion of influenza A virus in cell culture and applied it to a viral population carrying a diverse genetic barcode. Across this simplified cellular landscape, we found that spatial expansion produces a patchwork of distinct viral subpopulations. We then evaluated the consequences for population structure of two modulators of viral dispersal: extracellular viscosity and a common polymorphism in the viral attachment protein. Both physical constraint and viral phenotype altered the extent of genetic bottlenecking and spatial heterogeneity that developed during expansion, indicating that environmental features and viral traits that modulate dispersal also modulate viral population composition, diversity and evolution.

title: Dietary omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids interact with select gut microbes to produce bioactive metabolites found in infant gut metabolomes
content: Gut microbes metabolize nutrients in infant diets, producing compounds that play roles in host health. Long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (LCPUFAs) are an important component of infant diets, supporting neurological development and immune regulation. Emerging evidence demonstrates that gut microbes, alongside the host, participate in the metabolism of dietary lipids, highlighting an underexplored avenue for LCPUFA biology. In this work, alkyne-tagged eicosapentaenoic acid (EPAALK) was used to investigate interactions between LCPUFAs and the gut microbiota. Flow cytometry and comparative metabolomics identified gut microbial EPA interactors in the ileum of mice. Further comparative metabolomics analysis identified the conversion of EPA to N-acyl amino acids, including attachment to phenylalanine (EP-Phe) and leucine (EP-Leu). Targeted analysis of ex vivo stool cultures determined that EP-Phe and EP-Leu are produced by gut bacteria. A survey of lipid-relevant infant gut bacteria determined various flow cytometry-confirmed EPA-microbe interactions and identified Enterococcus faecalis, Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, and Clostridium bifermentans as competent producers of EP-Phe or EP-Leu. Thus, both novel metabolites from diet-derived inputs and microbial producers of these metabolites were identified. Together, this highlights important microbiome-centric and mechanistic consequences of LCPUFA consumption and emphasizes that the gut microbiome may be an important consideration in targeted supplementation strategies.

title: Evolutionary expansion of the bacterial ompW gene family enables functional diversification during host adaptation
content: The outer membrane protein W (OmpW) family comprises minor porins essential for environmental adaptation and host interactions in Gram-negative bacteria. However, ompW is conventionally treated as a ubiquitous single-copy gene, masking its true evolutionary complexity. Through comprehensive phylogenetic analysis across thousands of reference genomes, we reveal that ompW is present in nearly half of Gram-negative lineages, exhibiting a patchy distribution governed by a birth-and-death model of evolution with recurrent duplications and horizontal transfer. Notably, copy number expansions concentrate in lineages associated with eukaryotic hosts, linking paralog accumulation to niche adaptation. Experimental validation in Acinetobacter baumannii reveals four distinct loci that maintain high structural conservation despite sequence divergence, yet undergo profound functional specialization spanning from baseline physiological maintenance to modulating host colonization and persistence in vitro and in vivo. These findings dismantle the single-copy paradigm, demonstrating that widespread gene family expansion and paralog diversification drive the phenotypic plasticity required for bacteria to colonize hostile host environments.

title: Five decades of human H1N1 evolution reveal conserved glycan receptor specificity
content: H1N1 influenza viruses have circulated continuously among human populations for five decades. During evolution, the hemagglutinin has accumulated amino acid substitutions in and around the receptor-binding site (RBS), mainly due to antigenic pressure, potentially altering receptor recognition and binding profiles. Here, we investigated the glycan-binding properties of H1N1 strains collected from 1977 through 2024 using ELISA, flow cytometry, and tissue histochemistry to characterize changes in receptor-binding specificity over time. Across the strains examined, we observe a recurring preference for binding 2,6-sialylated di-LacNAc N-glycans. Binding to 2,3-sialylated glycans was generally undetectable, although A/Hongkong/117/1977 and A/New Caledonia/20/1999 bind chicken tracheal tissues. Interestingly, post-pandemic H1N1 viruses fluctuate in their relative binding avidities. The responsible amino acids, in turn, have different effects in pre-pandemic HA proteins. We also report a classical egg-adapted H1N1 mutant that shows null binding across platforms. These findings highlight the contribution of RBS mutations during initial adaptation and evolution of human H1N1 influenza viruses to glycan-binding properties, which, in contrast to H3N2 viruses, never fail to bind glycans that correlate with avian erythrocyte hemagglutination.

title: Gain-of-function mutations in the RodZ juxtamembrane domain promote Rod system activity in Escherichia coli
content: The peptidoglycan (PG) cell wall protects bacteria from osmotic lysis and determines their shape. In rod-shaped bacteria, the lateral wall is elongated by the Rod system (elongasome). This synthetic machine is built around the RodA-PBP2 PG synthase complex, the actin-like protein MreB, and the accessory proteins MreC, MreD, and RodZ. Notably, RodZ shares a similar domain organization with FtsN, an essential division protein that triggers PG synthesis by the division apparatus (divisome). Both are single pass transmembrane proteins that bind actin-like proteins in the cytoplasm and have largely unstructured periplasmic regions capped by small, folded C-terminal domains. We therefore investigated whether RodZ might function like FtsN in activating the Rod system.
